trial_title: POST-APPROVAL STUDY of TRANSCAROTID ARTERY REVASCULARIZATION in PATIENTS With SIGNIFICANT CAROTID ARTERY DISEASE
brief_summary: The ROADSTER 2 Study is intended to evaluate real world usage of the ENROUTE Transcarotid Stent when used with the ENROUTE Transcarotid Neuroprotection System by physicians of varying experience with the transcarotid technique.

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient must meet one of the following criteria regarding neurological symptom status and degree of stenosis:
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has significant bilateral carotid stenosis (80% on the right and 90% on the left) and a history of a prior cerebrovascular accident, which meets the criteria for symptomatic status.

eligibility_table.criterion: Symptomatic: Stenosis must be >50% as determined by an angiogram and the patient has a history of stroke (minor or non-disabling; NIHSS ≤4 or mRS ≤2), TIA and/or amaurosis fugax within 180 days of the procedure procedure ipsilateral to the carotid artery to be stented.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a history of a prior cerebrovascular accident (CVA) and significant stenosis (>50%), fulfilling the symptomatic criteria.

eligibility_table.criterion: OR Asymptomatic: Stenosis must be >80% as determined by angiogram without any neurological symptoms within the prior 180 days.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient does not meet the asymptomatic criteria as he has a history of stroke and is symptomatic.

eligibility_table.criterion: Target vessel must meet all requirements for ENROUTE Transcarotid Neuroprotection System and ENROUTE Stent System (refer to IFU for requirements).
eligibility_table.justification: Insufficient information provided to determine if the target vessel meets all requirements for the ENROUTE systems.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a carotid artery diameter of at least 4 mm to qualify for the ENROUTE Transcarotid Neuroprotection System and ENROUTE Stent System?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient has a discrete lesion located in the internal carotid artery (ICA) with or without involvement of the contiguous common carotid artery (CCA).
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has significant lesions in the internal carotid artery (ICA) as indicated by the stenosis.

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient is ≥18 years of age.
eligibility_table.justification: Patient age not recorded
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient currently 18 years of age or older?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient understands the nature of the procedure and has provided a signed informed consent using a form that has been reviewed and approved by the Institutional Review Board/Ethics Committee of the respective clinical site prior to the procedure. This will be obtained prior to participation in the study.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's understanding of the procedure and consent status is not provided.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient demonstrated an understanding of the nature of the Transcarotid Artery Revascularization procedure as assessed by a standardized comprehension assessment tool prior to providing signed informed consent?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient is willing to comply with the protocol requirements and return to the treatment center for all required clinical evaluations.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's willingness to comply with protocol requirements is not documented.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient able to attend all required clinical evaluations at the treatment center as outlined in the study protocol?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient must have a life expectancy ≥ 3 years at the time of the index procedure without contingencies related to other medical, surgical or endovascular intervention.
eligibility_table.justification: Category not evaluable deterministically
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a projected life expectancy of at least 3 years based on current health status and absence of contingencies related to other medical, surgical, or endovascular interventions?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient meets at least one of the surgical high-risk criteria listed below.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has multiple high-risk factors including CAD, PVD, and diabetes, which likely qualify him as surgical high-risk.

eligibility_table.criterion: Each potential patient must be screened to ensure that they do not meet any of the following exclusion criteria. This screening is to be based on known medical history and data available at the time of eligibility determination and enrollment.
eligibility_table.justification: No specific exclusion criteria have been assessed based on the provided medical history.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a history of any prior carotid artery interventions, such as carotid endarterectomy or stenting?

eligibility_table.justification: The presence of alternative sources of cerebral embolus is not clearly established in the provided information.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have any documented history of cardiac arrhythmias or other sources of cerebral emboli, such as atrial fibrillation, that could contribute to their cerebrovascular risk?

eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a documented history of chronic atrial fibrillation lasting ≥6 months?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient has had any episode of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation within the past 6 months, or history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation requiring chronic anticoagulation.
eligibility_table.justification: There is no mention of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, but lack of complete history leaves this criterion uncertain.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient experienced any episodes of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation within the past 6 months?

eligibility_table.criterion: Knowledge of cardiac sources of emboli. e.g. left ventricular aneurysm, intracardiac filling defect, cardiomyopathy, aortic or mitral prosthetic heart valve, calcific aortic stenosis, endocarditis, mitral stenosis, atrial septal defect, atrial septal aneurysm, or left atrial myxoma).
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has significant carotid artery disease, but no specific cardiac sources of emboli are documented.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have any documented cardiac sources of emboli, such as a left ventricular aneurysm or an atrial septal defect, that meet the established diagnostic criteria?

eligibility_table.criterion: Recently (<60 days) implanted heart valve (either surgically or endovascularly), which is a known source of emboli as confirmed on echocardiogram.
eligibility_table.justification: No recent heart valve implantation is mentioned, but the patient's complete cardiac history is not provided.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient undergone an echocardiogram within the last 60 days that confirms the presence of a recently implanted heart valve as a source of emboli?

eligibility_table.criterion: Abnormal angiographic findings: ipsilateral intracranial or extracranial arterial stenosis (as determined by angiography or CTA/MRA ≤ 6 months prior to index procedure) greater in severity than the lesion to be treated, cerebral aneurysm > 5 mm, AVM (arteriovenous malformation) of the cerebral vasculature, or other abnormal angiographic findings.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has significant carotid stenosis, but no recent angiographic findings are provided to assess this criterion.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have any ipsilateral intracranial or extracranial arterial stenosis greater than 80% as determined by angiography or CTA/MRA performed within the last 6 months?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient has a history of spontaneous intracranial hemorrhage within the past 12 months, or has had a recent (<7 days) stroke of sufficient size (on CT or MRI) to place him or her at risk of hemorrhagic conversion during the procedure.
eligibility_table.justification: There is a history of prior CVA, but no recent stroke or hemorrhage is documented.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient experienced a spontaneous intracranial hemorrhage within the past 12 months or a recent stroke of sufficient size on CT or MRI to place him at risk of hemorrhagic conversion during the procedure?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient had hemorrhagic transformation of an ischemic stroke within the past 60 days.
eligibility_table.justification: No recent hemorrhagic transformation is mentioned, but the patient's stroke history raises uncertainty.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient experienced a hemorrhagic transformation of an ischemic stroke within the past 60 days?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient with a history of major stroke attributable to either carotid artery (CVA or retinal embolus) with major neurological deficit (NIHSS ≥ 5 OR mRS ≥ 3) likely to confound study endpoints within 1 month of index procedure.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a history of stroke, but the severity and timing relative to the index procedure are unclear.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a history of a major stroke with an NIHSS score ≥ 5 or an mRS score ≥ 3 within 1 month of the index procedure?

eligibility_table.justification: The patient has significant carotid artery disease, which implies contralateral carotid artery occlusion.

eligibility_table.criterion: Tandem stenoses >70%
eligibility_table.justification: No lab values in patient profile
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have tandem stenoses in the carotid arteries that exceed 70%?

eligibility_table.justification: The patient has significant bilateral carotid stenosis but there is no specific mention of restenosis after carotid endarterectomy.

eligibility_table.justification: The patient has significant bilateral carotid artery stenosis (90% left ICA, 80% right ICA) which may require treatment.

eligibility_table.justification: The term 'Hostile Necks' is subjective and requires the investigator's assessment; no information is provided.

eligibility_table.justification: There is no mention of prior neck irradiation in the patient's history.

eligibility_table.criterion: Radical neck dissection
eligibility_table.justification: There is no indication of a radical neck dissection in the patient's prior treatments.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient undergone a radical neck dissection prior to enrollment in the study?

eligibility_table.criterion: Cervical spine immobility
eligibility_table.justification: Cervical spine immobility is not documented in the patient's profile.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient exhibit cervical spine immobility as defined by a range of motion less than 30 degrees in any direction?

eligibility_table.justification: The patient is male and does not meet the age criterion of being over 75 years.

eligibility_table.justification: No evidence of an intracranial tumor in the patient's profile.

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient has neurologic illnesses within the past two years characterized by fleeting or fixed neurologic deficit which cannot be distinguished from TIA or stroke

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient has had a TIA or amaurosis fugax within 48 hrs prior to the procedure

eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient experienced a myocardial infarction within the last 6 weeks but more than 72 hours prior to the procedure?

eligibility_table.justification: No lab values in patient profile

eligibility_table.justification: No mention of permanent contralateral cranial nerve injury.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient's serum creatinine level greater than 2.5 mg/dL?

eligibility_table.justification: No lab values in patient profile
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have ≥70% stenosis at the ostium of the common carotid artery (CCA) requiring revascularization?

eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient currently taking any medications that could indicate a risk of pregnancy or has the patient expressed any intention or possibility of becoming pregnant?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient has history of intolerance or allergic reaction to any of the study medications or stent materials (refer to stent IFU), including aspirin (ASA), ticlopidine, clopidogrel, statin or contrast media (that can't be pre medicated). Patients must be able to tolerate statins and a combination of ASA and ticlopidine or ASA and clopidogrel.
eligibility_table.justification: Patient is male, so this criterion does not apply.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient experienced any intolerance or allergic reaction to aspirin, ticlopidine, clopidogrel, statins, or contrast media that cannot be pre-medicated?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient must have a life expectancy <3 years without contingencies related to other medical, surgical, or interventional procedures as per the Wallaert Score and patients with primary, recurrent or metastatic malignancy who do not have independent assessment of life expectancy performed by the treating oncologist or an appropriate specialist other than the physician performing TCAR.
eligibility_table.justification: No history of intolerance or allergic reaction to study medications is provided.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the treating oncologist or an appropriate specialist other than the physician performing TCAR assessed the patient's life expectancy to confirm it is <3 years?
